signals.title: NZD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD/NOK presents a stark G10 performance split, with NZD registering a +0.902% 1W average gain across 4 pairs while NOK lags at -1.132% over 2 pairs, generating a 2.034% G10 spread. This performance divergence runs counter to underlying economic data surprises, as New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index sits at -25.1 (persistent data misses) while Norway's ESI holds at +8.7. Carry logic shows RBNZ at 2.75% (ON HOLD) vs Norges Bank at 4.5% (ON HOLD), leaving NZD at a nominal rate deficit against NOK. Despite NZD outperforming on short-term momentum, the combination of negative data surprises and a carry disadvantage leaves the bilateral rally vulnerable to repricing. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/NOK; short-term outperformance clashes with negative ESI and carry deficit. Catalyst: RBNZ Governor Orr speech at 22:00 UTC. Risk: Continued momentum extends the bilateral gap above 2.20% despite structural headwinds.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Vol Premium + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.95, holding below its SMA20 (157.93) and SMA200 (158.66) while remaining above the SMA50 at 157.27. Federal Reserve policy at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% generates a 266bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry differential favoring the dollar, sustaining underlying demand. However, Saxo options analytics reveal a strong put skew with 25d Risk Reversals at -2.05, paired with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.7% vs realized HV30 at 4.9% (a +1.8% vol risk premium). Institutional market participants are paying up for downside protection against potential BoJ policy acceleration, even as JPY COT leveraged funds net positioning remains short at -21,213 contracts (92nd percentile of its 52-week range, z=+1.46). A sustained break above 160.00 remains the historical threshold for intervention risk, though current spot action holds below that zone. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY; structural OIS carry dominance constrained by downside options hedging. Catalyst: US CPI release at 13:30 UTC (forecast 4.2% y/y). Risk: US inflation print misses consensus sharply, triggering a unwind of crowded JPY shorts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Repricing + Positioning + BEER Valuation
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3455, holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3360/1.3360/1.3420) with technical structure showing higher swing highs and lows. Bank of England policy rate at 4.00% (HIKING) vs Fed at 4.00% (ON HOLD) yields a neutral nominal spread, though SONIA vs SOFR OIS pricing provides a slight -9bp carry edge to Sterling. Positioning data shows Leveraged Funds net long at +32,686 contracts (WoW +12,670), reflecting institutional interest ahead of UK GDP data. Meanwhile, retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data shows a 63% short crowd, providing contrarian support to institutional longs. The BEER model flags fair value misvaluation with GBP/AUD rich at z=+2.94σ, while GBP/USD option 25d Risk Reversals reflect a mild put skew at -0.42. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; technical stack above moving average cluster supported by BoE rate stance. Catalyst: UK GDP q/q print at 07:00 UTC (forecast 0.8%). Risk: UK growth data misses expectations, breaching technical support at 1.3420.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Positioning + OIS Carry Advantage
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4108, maintaining position above its SMA20 (1.4061), SMA50 (1.4049), and SMA200 (1.3899) following a weak Canadian employment release. SOFR at 3.89% vs CORRA at 2.52% creates a +137bp OIS carry advantage supporting the USD leg, supported by Fed policy rate at 4.00% vs BoC at 2.50%. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short CAD at -85,289 contracts (18.5% long, pctl 25), while Retail sentiment data retail sentiment sits at an extreme 77% short bias (23% long). With retail heavily fading the upside move while institutional positioning remains net short CAD, price action continues to hold above key moving averages. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; rate differential and net-short CAD positioning favor upside continuation. Catalyst: US CPI release at 13:30 UTC. Risk: US CPI prints cooler than expected, prompting profit-taking back toward the 1.4061 SMA20 support.

signals.title: EUR/USD — COT Squeeze Risk + BEER Fair Value Misvaluation
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1238, positioned above its 20-day moving average (1.1198) but below the 50-day (1.1339) and 200-day (1.1542) SMAs. CFTC Leveraged Funds net positioning sits heavily short at -104,030 contracts (31.8% long, 52-week percentile 2, z=-1.80), indicating stretched institutional short positioning. The equilibrium model flags EUR/USD as significantly undervalued at z=-3.55σ below fair value (spot 1.1238 vs model 1.1389). Fed policy rate at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a +145bp SOFR-€STR OIS carry gap in favor of the dollar, limiting broad structural upside. However, the combination of extreme 52-week COT short percentiles and BEER model misvaluation creates asymmetric upside squeeze risk if macro headlines turn dovish for the USD. Trade bias: Neutral/Tactical Bullish EUR/USD; extreme COT short positioning creates squeeze potential against carry headwinds. Catalyst: US CPI print at 13:30 UTC. Risk: US CPI surprises to the upside, reinforcing the 145bp USD carry buffer and driving spot below 1.1198 SMA20.
